summary: Iteration 268 email-change flow: 14/14 backend tests passed. Verified request/verify/revoke endpoints, token hashing (sha256), 15-min expiry, 3/hour rate limit, session invalidation via tokenVersion increment, expired-token auto-cleanup, and login post-swap. Regression on canonical login + /api/settings + /api/auth/change-password intact. All disposable test users cleaned up; bookingtest@test.com/password123 preserved and login-verified.
critical_code_review_comments: auth.ts request-email-change increments emailChangeAttempts BEFORE the uniqueness (409) check, so a 409 still consumes a rate-limit slot. Non-critical but worth noting: a user typing an already-used email 3 times gets locked out for 1 hour. Consider moving the attempts++/persist step to AFTER the 409 uniqueness check, or only counting attempts that make it to token generation.

verify-email-change race guard returns 409 without clearing rate-limit fields (emailChangeAttempts/emailChangeWindowStart) even though pendingEmail/token/expiry are cleared. Minor inconsistency vs the success path which resets both to 0/null.

revoke-email-change is public and only requires the raw token — this is fine since the token is a 32-byte random secret sent only to the affected addresses. Response body is minimal ({success:true}) which is appropriate.

sendEmailChangeConfirmation on verify is fire-and-forget (.catch inline) which is correct — matches change-password idiom. sendEmailChangeVerification/Alert on request use try/await which briefly blocks the response by up to Resend timeout; consider making them fire-and-forget too for consistency and faster responses, but non-blocking as currently coded (won't fail the request).

test_credentials.canonical: bookingtest@test.com / password123 — RESTORED and login-verified (200) at end of run. tokenVersion=0, emailVerified=false (unchanged), all emailChange* fields null.
test_credentials.disposable_users_created: ~7 users with iter268_<hex>@example.com — all deleted via prisma cleanup (final deleteMany returned count=0 on second call, confirming clean state)

seed_data_creation: None permanent. All test users signed up on-the-fly with prefix 'iter268_' and deleted in session teardown.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Prisma helper script at /app/kolor-studio-v2/backend/scripts/iter268_prisma_helper.js supports: get/inject/inject-expired/verify-user/restore-email/reset-fields/cleanup. Backend runs on ts-node (no hot-reload); if you edit routes/auth.ts you must restart backend. Login does NOT require emailVerified. Resend emails 403 (unverified domain) in preview — audit logs in backend logs are '[EMAIL-CHANGE] Requested|Verified|Revoked user=<id>'. To test token flow without email delivery, POST /request-email-change first (validates auth/rate limit/uniqueness), then INJECT known raw token via prisma helper 'inject <email> <rawToken> <pendingEmail>'.
rca_of_any_issue:
No bugs found. All 8 feature specs from the review request executed and passed:
1. request-email-change (a-f): all 6 validation branches verified
2. Rate limit 4th → 429 with 'minutes' in message
3. verify-email-change garbage → 400; happy path via injected token → 200 with oldEmail/newEmail; all 5 change fields cleared; tokenVersion +1
4. Session invalidation: pre-verify /api/settings 200, post-verify 401 (same cookie)
5. Login new email 200, login old email 401
6. Revoke happy path 200 + fields cleared + email unchanged; double-revoke → 400
7. Expired-token GET verify → 400 'expired' + pending fields auto-cleared
8. Regression: canonical login+settings 200; change-password endpoint responds 401 to wrong currentPassword (not 500)
